answer: Proposed rule: each karst survey ID/day completes a 1,000,000-round hash chain seeded by a unique registry-issued ID/day nonce and its map digest (jade = safe cells; violet = hazards). The registry recomputes it; missing or wrong results deny listing. Assuming no hash shortcuts, 10 IDs require 10,000,000 rounds despite shared chips or parallel runs. Power costs recur; chips are reusable capital; no stake. Fast chips cheapen entry; checking repeats the work. This meters computation, not map accuracy or distinct owners.
